title: The misdirected personal-data file — question explanation
learningObjective: Limit exposure, preserve relevant facts and notify responsible privacy/security roles
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A staff member emails a spreadsheet with personal identifiers to an external recipient with a similar name. The recipient has not yet confirmed deletion.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Limit exposure, preserve relevant facts and notify responsible privacy/security roles
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option B: Notify the privacy/security incident channel promptly, preserve message details, request containment through approved procedures and let authorized roles assess notification obligations. Prompt escalation allows the organization to assess exposure, legal/contractual duties and necessary containment.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: A deletion request may help but does not replace formal incident assessment, notification and evidence preservation. Option C: Recall may fail or the recipient may already have accessed or copied the file. Option D: Further disclosure increases exposure and is not an incident-response control.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Report immediately, preserve relevant facts without unnecessary copying, request approved recipient-side containment and follow the privacy team’s incident process. A misdirected data disclosure is an incident to assess even when accidental and even if recall is attempted.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.

Use only fictional names, domains, screens and values. Never render real secrets, OTPs, account data or real target systems.
